catalog_quote: On the basis of new fieldwork data, I arrived at an alternative analysis of the word prosodic system of Ma'ya, with only three tonemes, restricted to the final syllable, and contrastive lexical stress (either penultimate or final). ... Assuming that this analysis is correct, Ma'ya is the only tone language in the world that has been demonstrated to feature lexically contrastive stress. [p.2] ... Ma'ya features three paradigmatically contrastive tones. To begin with, there are the High and the Rising tonemes (/3/ and /12/ respectively). The distribution of these tonemes is limited to the final syllable of content word roots. Paradoxically, lexical stress functions as a third paradigmatically contrastive element, in contrast with the High and Rise tonemes. ... Lexical stress is syntagmatically contrastive in polysyllabic words, either on the penultimate or on the final syllable. [p.53] ..…
sweep_summary: Both sweep items are Glottolog duplicates of the catalog's own deciding source, Remijsen's 2001 LOT 49 dissertation (Glottolog dates one copy 2002 with a dead Papuaweb URL; the other is the MPI handle copy behind a bot wall). The open LOT PDF is on file and was re-read: it confirms the 'lexical' coding (contrastive penult vs final stress, minimal pairs, acoustic support) and the catalog's secondary rule (contrast confined to penult-/a/ words; constraints I-III pp.106-107, 122). Additional stress-relevant works found via Crossref and the Glottolog langdoc list but not in the item list: Remijsen 2002 LabPhon 7 chapter (published version of ch. III; paywalled, medium priority) and Remijsen 2001 Language and Speech (dialectal tone variation; paywalled, low), plus van der Leeden 1983/1993 (print only; earlier four-toneme analysis that Remijsen supersedes), van der Leeden 1997 and Kawira 1986 (not found). Arnold 2018 (on file) is a consistent secondary summary. No change to the catalog is warranted; no new statement supersedes the current source.

new_statements.quote: I. If a polysyllabic word has a vowel other than /a/ in the penultimate syllable, it can only have penultimate stress. Alternatively, when a polysyllabic word has the vowel /a/ in the penultimate syllable, then stress is contrastive, either on the penultimate or on the final syllable. II. If a polysyllabic word has a vowel other than /a/ in the penultimate syllable, the vowels of penultimate and final syllables are usually the same. ... III. Words with penultimate stress can only have a High toneme; words with final stress can have either the High or the Rise tonemes. [pp.106-107] ... Contrastive stress, therefore, is limited to words with the penultimate syllable vowel /a/, and mostly with final vowel also being /a/ [p.122]

new_statements.reading: Salawati Ma'ya has lexically contrastive stress restricted to a two-syllable right-edge window (penult or final), coexisting with three final-syllable tonemes; the contrast is only live when the penult vowel is /a/, otherwise stress is penultimate. This is the same source the catalog already cites and the catalog's 'lexical' kind plus its secondary rule already encode exactly these passages ( correction of 2026-09-12). Nothing read in this sweep is more authoritative or more first-hand.

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Remijsen 2001 LOT dissertation at the stated pages (p.2, p.53; sub-regularities pp.105-106; secondary locators p.18, p.49 also verified). The source is the definitive fieldwork-based phonological and instrumental study of Ma'ya word prosody by the specialist on the language, superseding van der Leeden 1993; no reference grammar has been published, and the later literature (Arnold 2018, fetched sources, pp.9-10) restates the same analysis: lexical tone confined to the final syllable, lexical stress contrastive between penult and final. Coding 'lexical', right edge, is exactly what the source says. Wishlist items are low-priority corroboration (refereed versions, the superseded competing analysis), none likely to change the coding.

sources.note: This Glottolog entry IS the catalog's deciding source (same dissertation, Glottolog dates it 2002 and points at a dead Papuaweb mirror). Salawati Ma'ya: three final-syllable tonemes plus lexically contrastive stress on penult or final syllable (minimal pairs /'mana3/ 'light' vs /ma'na3/ 'grease', p.54); contrast confined to words with penult /a/, non-/a/ penult entails penultimate stress (pp.106-107, 122); acoustic correlates duration, intensity, vowel quality, not f0 (p.54).
